brief: Pictet's Monday Kick-off recaps a steadier start to the week after last week's selloff, with AI and momentum names rebounding Friday on technical and positioning factors. Thursday was one of the toughest sessions in months: the post-midterm Democratic sweep hit big tech hard, sending the Nasdaq into correction, cutting roughly USD 1T from the Mag 7, and giving semiconductors their worst day since March 2020 on AI investment-constraint and growth concerns. Friday's strong October jobs report then sold off fixed income, pushing the 2-year Treasury yield up 14bp to 4.25% as traders priced a 70% probability of a December hike. Oil still fell on the week on hopes of Middle East de-escalation, despite Trump weighing renewed Iran strikes. The firm's Exposure Optimisation Model trimmed global equity exposure to 70% from 71%, with Europe's score jumping to 90% from 69% while Asia fell to 46% from 60% on a Shenzhen cut to 0%. House themes: tech and semis volatility could stay elevated until support holds. Health Care is rotating into leadership on the tech selloff. European banks may see a tactical rebound after French credit stress. Quality dispersion is widening as Momentum and High Beta lose leadership.
